rounds.name: Recruiter Screen
rounds.focus: Background, motivation for Microsoft, basic role fit. Note: Microsoft historically uses 'Program Manager' as its core product-definition title (see project_management track below); the separate 'Product Manager' title at Microsoft leans more toward GTM, positioning, and marketing strategy for a product line. India note: Hyderabad and Bangalore are Microsoft's largest India R&D hubs (Azure, Windows, Bing, Dynamics, M365); loops there follow the same global structure and are commonly fully virtual.
questions: Walk me through your resume and your path into product
Why Microsoft, and why this team?
What's your favorite Microsoft product, and how would you improve it?
Tell me about a time you launched or positioned a product in market
Where do you see yourself in five years?

rounds.name: Hiring Manager Screen
rounds.focus: Deeper behavioral questions with light product thinking
rounds.evaluates: Communication quality, product reasoning, experience alignment with team needs
questions: Tell me about a product launch you owned end-to-end
Describe a time you had to make the case for a product's positioning against a competitor
How do you balance customer needs with business constraints?
Tell me about a time you were unable to meet a customer's needs - what happened?
Discuss a challenge or roadblock you faced on a recent product initiative

rounds.name: Product Design
rounds.focus: Ambiguous product problem, GTM/positioning trade-offs, ecosystem-scale reasoning
rounds.evaluates: Problem definition, user prioritization, trade-off reasoning, business/technical lifecycle planning
questions: How would you improve Microsoft Teams for hybrid meetings?
Design a new feature for Microsoft 365 aimed at small businesses in India
How would you position a new Copilot feature against a competitor's AI assistant?
Walk me through how you'd launch a product into a market with an established incumbent
How would you decide whether to build, buy, or partner for a new capability?
Design an onboarding experience for a first-time Azure customer

rounds.name: Behavioral / Collaboration
rounds.focus: Leadership, cross-functional collaboration, customer empathy, influence
rounds.evaluates: Leadership, communication, decision-making, customer obsession, growth mindset
questions: Tell me about a time you had to influence a decision without direct authority
Describe a time you disagreed with an engineering partner on scope
Tell me about a time you received difficult feedback and how you responded
How do you handle ambiguity when requirements keep changing?
Tell me about a time you had to say no to a stakeholder's request
Describe a situation where you demonstrated a growth mindset after a setback

rounds.name: As Appropriate (AA) Round
rounds.format: 30-45 min interview with a senior manager, only triggered if earlier rounds went well
rounds.focus: Adaptive, gap-closing round tailored to whatever signal is weakest from earlier interviews (technical depth, strategy, or culture fit); if signal is strong, the interviewer also 'sells' the candidate on the team
rounds.evaluates: Whatever is unresolved from prior rounds - commonly strategic thinking and culture fit
questions: Tell me more about your product philosophy and how you approach ambiguity
What questions do you have about the team, the product, or Microsoft's direction?
How would you describe your working style to a new manager?
What's a strategic bet you'd make for this product area over the next 2 years?
Why should we hire you over other strong candidates in this loop?
What are you most excited about, and what's your biggest concern about this role?

rounds.name: Recruiter Screen
rounds.focus: Communication, cultural fit, motivation. Note: at Microsoft, 'Program Manager' is the traditional, core product-definition role (spec ownership, working daily with engineering) - closer to a PM/TPM hybrid elsewhere - while 'Technical Program Manager' is used for more infrastructure/cross-org execution-heavy programs (common in Azure/Cloud+AI). India note: onsite loops in Hyderabad/Bangalore commonly run all rounds back-to-back in a single day, including the AA round.
questions: Why Microsoft, and what appeals to you about this Program Manager role?
Walk me through your background and the programs/products you've owned
Why this particular product area or team?
Tell me about your experience working directly with engineering teams

rounds.name: Systems Design
rounds.focus: Program/product-level system design and architecture reasoning
rounds.evaluates: Technical depth, systems thinking, scalability reasoning
questions: Design a high-level system for a notification service used across Microsoft 365
How would you design a feature rollout system that supports staged/ring-based deployment?
Walk me through the architecture considerations for a multi-tenant SaaS feature
What trade-offs would you weigh when designing for reliability versus speed of shipping?
Design a data pipeline to power a new product's usage analytics

rounds.name: Data Structures, Algorithms & Data Sourcing
rounds.focus: Core CS fundamentals and data-sourcing reasoning appropriate to a technical PM/TPM
rounds.evaluates: Technical/coding fluency, data fluency, structured problem-solving
questions: Walk through a data structure choice you'd make for a specific product scenario and why
How would you source and validate data to make a product decision when no dashboard exists?
Solve a basic algorithmic problem and discuss its time/space complexity
How would you design a database schema for tracking feature usage across teams?
What questions would you ask before trusting a metric reported by another team?

rounds.name: Behavioral / Leadership
rounds.format: 45-50 min 1:1 onsite interview (often with hiring manager or head of group)
rounds.focus: Customer obsession, growth mindset, cross-team collaboration under ambiguity
rounds.evaluates: Leadership, customer obsession, growth mindset, collaboration
questions: Tell me about a time you had to rally a team around a decision they initially resisted
Describe a situation where you had to manage a program with conflicting stakeholder goals
Tell me about a time you failed to meet a customer's needs - what did you learn?
How do you handle ambiguity when a product's direction from leadership is unclear?
Discuss a challenge or roadblock you faced and how you overcame it
Tell me about a time you had to hold engineering accountable to a commitment

rounds.name: As Appropriate (AA) Round
rounds.format: 30-45 min interview with a Principal PM or senior executive; often the final round of the day
rounds.focus: Gap-closing round on product vision, goals, roadmap, and Microsoft fit; also discusses compensation/level fit in India loops
rounds.evaluates: Whatever signal is weakest from earlier rounds - typically vision, technology understanding, and process maturity
questions: Walk me through your product vision for an area you've owned
How do you think about setting goals and measuring a roadmap's success?
What's your process for turning ambiguous leadership direction into an execution plan?
How would you use data to defend a roadmap decision to skeptical stakeholders?
What questions do you have about the team or Microsoft's direction?
Why should we hire you for this role specifically?
